item.title: Who are the Chase Ultimate Rewards airline and hotel transfer partners?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.64
Who are the Chase Ultimate Rewards airline and hotel transfer partners? Editor's Note Chase Ultimate Rewards is one of the most valuable rewards currencies you can have in your wallet. Aside from possibly earning 1 to 10 points per dollar spent on select Chase-branded credit cards, you can maximize their value by transferring your hard-earned Ultimate Rewards points to one of the issuer's 14 loyalty partners. Whether you want to book a flight to Europe, save on a domestic trip or stay at a high-end hotel, redeeming your Ultimate Rewards points via transfer partners can be a lucrative way to spend (and even save) your Chase points. Here is everything to know about Chase Ultimate Rewards' transfer partners. Who are the Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer partners? You can transfer Ultimate Rewards points to 10 airline programs: - Aer Lingus AerClub - Air Canada Aeroplan - Air France-KLM Flying Blue - British Airways Club - Iberia Club - JetBlue TrueBlue - Singapore KrisFlyer - Southwest Rapid Rewards - United MileagePlus - Virgin Atlantic Flying Club Chase also partners with four hotel programs: Chase points transfer to partners at a 1:1 ratio, with one exception. New Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees) cardholders who applied on or after June 15 can transfer Chase points to World of Hyatt at a 4:3 rate. Existing Sapphire Preferred cardholders can continue transferring points to Hyatt at a 1:1 rate through Sept. 30, before moving to a 4:3 rate on Oct. 1. For Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (see rates and fees) cardholders, transfers to World of Hyatt remain 1:1 through Sept. 30. Beginning Oct. 1, both existing cardholders and new applicants will transfer Chase points to Hyatt at a 4:3 rate. Transfers must be made in increments of 1,000. However, Chase occasionally offers transfer bonuses to partners, which can yield even higher value for your redemptions. How long do Chase Ultimate Rewards transfers take? Most transfers from Chase Ultimate Rewards to its partner programs are instantaneous. However, in our most recent testing, transfers to Singapore KrisFlyer took about 48 hours. Delays can happen when transferring your points for some simple reasons as well. To facilitate the transfer process, ensure that the name on your Ultimate Rewards account matches the one on your loyalty program account. Additionally, make sure you have signed up for a loyalty program in advance, as transferring to a new account may also cause a delay. How do you transfer Chase Ultimate Rewards points to partners? You can easily transfer Chase points online. First, log in to your Chase account and navigate to the Ultimate Rewards portal. In the "Travel" drop-down menu, select "Transfer points to partners" to access the main transfer page. You will then see the list of transfer partners and any current transfer bonuses. Select your desired transfer partner, link your external account if you have not already done so, select the number of Ultimate Rewards points you wish to transfer and then submit the transfer. Remember, Ultimate Rewards transfers cannot be reversed, so it's best to wait until you have a specific redemption in mind before transferring points. Related: Chase Ultimate Rewards points: How to redeem for maximum value What are the best Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer partners? If you prefer to transfer your points to one of the 10 airline program partners, the best redemption options for you may vary depending on factors such as which airlines fly to and from the destinations you wish to visit and which airlines you prefer to fly. However, there are notable sweet spots with certain airline transfer options, especially those programs that have retained award charts. Here are some of our favorite partners to book using Chase points. Book a round-trip flight to Madrid via Iberia Club Flying from the U.S. to Spain doesn't have to set you back thousands of dollars. Round-trip, off-peak flights from New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) to Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport (MAD) will only set you back 32,000 Avios in basic economy, 59,000 Avios in premium economy and 81,000 Avios in business class (plus applicable taxes and fees) when you transfer your Chase points to Iberia Club, though the airline sometimes runs award discounts that can mean even cheaper seats. Considering that most airlines charge at least 60,000 miles for a one-way business-class award to Europe, an off-peak business-class flight to and from Madrid booked via Iberia Club for just 32,000 Avios round-trip is excellent value. Book flights to Hawaii via British Airways Club Did you know that you can book American Airlines and Alaska Airlines flights with Chase points? Though the carriers' loyalty programs are not direct transfer partners of Chase, you can book flights on these airlines by transferring your Ultimate Rewards points to British Airways Club and then redeem British Airways Avios for award flights on its Oneworld partners. Typically, you can find saver-level award space from American's and Alaska's West Coast gateways to various airports in Hawaii in economy for 44,000 Avios round-trip, or 22,000 Avios one-way, plus minimal taxes and fees. Book lie-flat business-class seats to London via Virgin Atlantic Flying Club Is London calling? Though Virgin Atlantic Flying Club prices its award seats dynamically, the loyalty program offers saver fares for low-demand travel dates. If you're flexible and come across availability, you could score lie-flat business-class seats from JFK to London's Heathrow Airport (LHR) for as few as 29,000 points with one recent deal, though note that taxes, fees and carrier-imposed surcharges of around $700 one-way are also payable. If you're looking to be more thrifty with your hard-earned points, you can fly the exact same route in economy for as few as 6,000 points (plus about $165 in taxes and fees), depending on the direction. You can use Virgin Atlantic's reward seat checker to find saver fares or an award booking platform like Seats.aero to search dates and prices. However, be sure to confirm award availability with the airline prior to booking a seat. Book a stay at a top-tier Hyatt hotel via World of Hyatt You can also get great value from your Chase Ultimate Rewards points by transferring them to World of Hyatt. The hotel loyalty program offers a very appealing award chart, broken into 8 hotel categories and 5 rate tiers from Lowest to Top. By transferring your Chase points to Hyatt, you can book some of the most luxurious Park Hyatt properties in the entire portfolio, including the Park Hyatt London River Thames, starting at 35,000 points per night during the Lowest dates. Just remember that after the 4:3 rate for Chase to Hyatt transfers goes into effect, you'll need to transfer 47,000 Chase points to World of Hyatt to make that 35,000 point booking. What are Chase Ultimate Rewards points worth? TPG values Ultimate Rewards points at 2.05 cents apiece, per our September 2026 valuations, but you can find even more value by transferring points to airline and hotel partners. However, you'll get different values for Chase points when you pursue other redemption options. For example, since the addition of Points Boost, Ultimate Rewards points can be worth up to 2.5 cents per point on select Chase Travel℠ bookings if you hold the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) or the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees). You can receive up to 1.5 cents per point through the portal if you hold the Chase Sapphire Preferred or the Ink Business Preferred. How can you earn Chase Ultimate Rewards points? You can earn Chase points depending on the specific Chase credit card you carry. The following cards earn fully transferable Ultimate Rewards points: - Chase Sapphire Reserve: Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business: Earn 200,000 bonus points after spending $30,000 on purchases in the first six months from account opening. - Chase Sapphire Preferred Card: Earn 75,000 bonus points after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Ink Business Preferred Credit Card: Earn 100,000 bonus points after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. However, if you have an Ultimate Rewards points-earning card, you can effectively convert your cash-back rewards into Ultimate Rewards points, too. For this reason, having more than one Chase card can make sense to maximize your earning and redeeming potential. Here are the four cash-back Chase cards that offer the opportunity to convert the cash-back rewards you earn into fully transferable Ultimate Rewards points as a cardholder of one of the above points-earning Chase cards: - Chase Freedom Flex® (see rates and fees): Earn $200 cash back after spending $500 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Chase Freedom Unlimited® (see rates and fees): Earn $200 cash back after spending $500 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. - Ink Business Cash® Credit Card (see rates and fees): Earn $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. - Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card (see rates and fees): Earn $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. Bottom line If you value the flexibility of choosing from 10 airline partners and four hotel partners, Chase Ultimate Rewards is one of the best points programs out there. In the age of no-notice devaluations by some loyalty programs, it is smart to earn Ultimate Rewards points via credit card welcome offers, category bonuses and everyday spending and then keep your points until you are ready to transfer and book with an airline or hotel partner, which is why earning Chase Ultimate Rewards points is an exceptionally savvy travel strategy. Related: The power of the Chase Trifecta: Maximize your earnings with 3 cards TPG featured card | 5x | Earn 5x on travel purchased through Chase Travel℠. | | 3x | Earn 3x on dining, vacation homes, gas & EV charging, top streaming services and online groceries (excluding Walmart, Target, and wholesale clubs). | | 2x | Earn 2x on all other travel purchases. | | 1x | Earn 1x on all other purchases. |

item.title: This tiny airline lets you skip TSA and fly between small airports for less
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.07
This tiny airline lets you skip TSA and fly between small airports for less I had never before been to an airport where I could arrive 20 minutes before my flight, park for free, walk straight into the terminal and board a nine-seat plane without passing through the typical commercial airport security process. But that's exactly what happened when I flew SeaPort Airlines between Spokane, Washington, and Seattle this summer. What is SeaPort? "Please don't tell anyone about this," fellow passenger Ken Batali pleaded, moments after we disembarked a SeaPort Airlines Pilatus PC-12 turboprop plane, grabbed our bags off the cart and walked through a silent terminal to an empty curb. Along with five other passengers — more people than usual, according to our pilot — we had flown on one of SeaPort's fairly new scheduled flights between Felts Field (SFF) airport in Spokane, Washington, and King County International Airport - Boeing Field (BFI), just 5 miles south of downtown Seattle. Instead of flying from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) to Spokane International Airport (GEG), SeaPort Airlines operates between smaller general aviation airports (which primarily serve private, corporate, charter and other non-major-airline flights); these airports are often much closer to city centers than their larger, commercial counterparts. So, no one had to show up more than 20 minutes before the Spokane-Seattle flight, pay for parking or pass through Transportation Security Administration-style security screening. There was no limit on liquids, and each passenger could bring up to 50 pounds of baggage, including a small pet in a carrier, for free. Batali, who lives about 30 miles north of Seattle, has been flying to Spokane regularly for work. He loves that the SeaPort flights from small airports save him time and hassle when compared to typical commercial flights. How do the prices compare? Batali said he noticed that trying to book a flight weeks in advance on SeaPort usually costs more than booking in advance on either Alaska Airlines or Delta Air Lines (which fly larger planes between the larger airports, SEA and GEG). When we compared commercial versus SeaPort prices, there was about a $50 difference. However, it's the last-minute bookings — a reality of business travel — where Seaport has made Batali's life much easier. "Booking last minute, as I usually do, I can always get a seat, and the ticket price is the same as last minute on Alaska," he said. If word about SeaPort gets out, he's worried it will be more difficult (and more expensive) to make a last-minute reservation on a nine-seat aircraft. And word does seem to be getting out. On our flight, a three-member finance team from a major Spokane company was testing the time and cost benefit of SeaPort's approximately one-hour, Spokane-to-Seattle flight between the two general aviation airports. "The ticket price was pretty much the same, we all had time to have dinner at home, we got free parking, and we'll have lower Uber fees in Seattle because we land closer to downtown," one team member told me. SeaPort Airlines — a Juneau, Alaska-based carrier — began offering scheduled flights between Seattle's Boeing Field and Spokane's Felts Field in March 2026. Flights between Boeing Field and the general aviation provider next to Portland International Airport (PDX) began in May 2025. (A previous incarnation of SeaPort served that route between 2008 and 2016). And this summer, SeaPort offered seasonal service to the general aviation terminal in Redmond, Oregon, near Redmond Municipal Airport (RDM). What was it like to fly SeaPort? In August, I became curious about this tiny airline whose tagline is: "It's about time." So, I took scheduled flights between all four Pacific Northwest cities that SeaPort Airlines serves. Out of habit, I showed up an hour before each flight, which I discovered was far too early since there's no metal detector, formal identification check or other security screening. All bags get weighed, but otherwise, the preflight experience consisted of the pilot and co-pilot greeting passengers in the waiting area, checking names against a list, walking the group out to the plane and loading the bags into a netted area at the rear of the plane. Walking the few steps from the terminal to the plane for the first flight, I stopped and took a step back. Not just because I wanted to snap a photo of the airplane, but because I realized it's been a very long time since I've flown in a small plane — and this Pilatus PC-12 turboprop plane looked very small. I followed my very calm-looking fellow passengers onto the plane and took a seat by the exit door. While not fancy, there was a definite private-jet feeling. The pilot swiveled around from the cockpit to give the safety briefing before takeoff. Like Batali and the finance team from the Spokane company that requested anonymity, my fellow passengers on each flight were mostly business travelers. On my flight from Redmond through Portland and home to Seattle, I met first-time passenger Brian Hayvaz. Hayvaz is the vice president of operations for Aircare International, a Tacoma, Washington-based company that provides emergency training for the crews that staff business and private jets. The SeaPort Airlines flight had popped up in his regular commercial flight search, and he'd booked a seat right away. "I assumed SeaPort was going to be too expensive, but the pricing was competitive. It's easy and convenient," Hayvaz said. "I'd fly this airline to other destinations if I could." In addition to company executives, Andy Kline, SeaPort Airlines' marketing manager, said the passenger makeup is proving a bit surprising. "We get electricians, roofers, project managers and contractors," Kline said. "It's a lot of people who need to get to job sites in other cities and a lot of people who charge by the hour." It's certainly a different, more convenient and often less expensive way to travel regionally. No security screening? The "no TSA-style security screening" aspect of SeaPort Airlines' service is, for some, one of the more appealing and intriguing aspects of the flight experience. Airline staff watches for hazardous materials and issues, such as passengers who may be unfit for travel, Kline said. He also added that relaxed security screening is allowed because the airline is a Part 135 carrier under Federal Aviation Administration regulations, which govern scheduled service carriers operating planes carrying nine or fewer passengers, with some exceptions. But as Hansford Smith, vice president of risk management at Silver Air Private Jets, noted: "The absence of a traditional checkpoint does not mean there is no security screening." There are a variety of reasons why TSA-type screening may or may not apply to passengers on flights operated by other Part 135 operators offering scheduled service, such as Cape Air, JSX, Boutique Air, Tradewind Aviation, Mokulele Airlines and Kenmore Airlines. "In many, if not most, instances, it is a case-by-case determination by the TSA as to what the required security protocols will be," Mark A. Dombroff, partner and aviation attorney at Fox Rothschild LLP, said. He notes that the determining factors may range from the airports involved and whether passengers board or deplane through the sterile or secure areas of the airport, to the maximum certificated weight and seating capacity of the aircraft.

item.title: Bank of America Travel Center guide: How to book travel and redeem rewards
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.05
Bank of America Travel Center guide: How to book travel and redeem rewards If you didn't know Bank of America had a travel portal, you're probably not alone. The Bank of America Travel Center doesn't get nearly as much attention as travel portals from issuers like Chase, Capital One and Citi. But there's more to BofA Travel than you might expect, including plenty of ways to book travel and use your rewards. Here's how the portal works and what to know before you book. What is the Bank of America Travel Center? The Bank of America Travel Center — which you'll see referred to as BofA Travel within the booking experience — lets eligible cardholders book flights, hotels, rental cars and activities. Bank of America revamped the Travel Center in July 2026. The new portal, powered by Rocket Travel by Agoda, significantly expanded the selection of hotels, flights, rental cars and activities available to book. The update wasn't just cosmetic. Now, the portal has better search and filtering tools, more detailed hotel information and the ability to mix and match airlines on round-trip bookings. Eligible cardholders can even combine rewards with a credit or debit card payment. Who can access the Bank of America Travel Center? Exactly what you can do in the Travel Center depends on which Bank of America card is in your wallet. Some cardholders can book travel and redeem rewards through the portal, while others can only make paid bookings. How you access the Travel Center varies by card, too. Here's what access currently looks like for eligible personal Bank of America cards: | Card | Booking and payment options | Where to find BofA Travel | |---|---|---| | | Book with rewards and/or card payments | Online Banking or mobile app | | | Book with rewards and/or card payments | Online Banking or mobile app | | | Book with card payments | Online Banking | | | Book with card payments | Erica in the mobile app or Search in Online Banking | | | Book with card payments | Erica in the mobile app or Search in Online Banking | | BankAmericard Rewards® credit card (closed to new applicants) | Book with rewards and/or card payments | Online Banking | The information for the BankAmericard Rewards credit card and Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite credit card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Related: Best Bank of America credit cards of September 2026 How to use the Bank of America Travel Center Once you're in BofA Travel, here's what to expect when making a booking. How to book flights through the Bank of America Travel Center To search for flights, enter your origin, destination, travel dates and number of travelers. BofA Travel supports one-way, round-trip and multicity searches, and you can search by economy, premium economy, business or first class. Once your results load, you can filter your options and compare flights from more than 170 airlines. On round-trip itineraries, your outbound and return flights don't need to be on the same carrier. Each flight includes a tab with baggage information and a link to the airline's baggage policies. Pay close attention to the fare you're selecting, since restrictions and included benefits vary by fare type. There can be some airline-specific quirks, too. When I selected a Frontier Airlines flight, BofA Travel warned me that the flight would be managed directly by Frontier and that I'd need to contact the airline for any changes or assistance after booking. You also can't select your seat before booking, at least for the airlines I tested, which included Frontier, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines and United Airlines. Each time, the booking page told me I'd need to contact the airline for seat selection. Don't forget to add your frequent flyer number during booking, since flights booked through BofA Travel can still earn airline miles and elite-qualifying credits based on the airline's fare rules. Once you've entered your information and reviewed your flight and fare details, select "Continue to payment" to finish booking. How to book hotels through the Bank of America Travel Center To search for a hotel, select "Hotels" and enter your destination, travel dates and number of travelers. Then hit "Search hotels." There are more than half a million properties available worldwide, ranging from traditional hotels to apartments, hostels and other accommodations. So, whether you're looking for a five-star hotel, a budget stay or something with more space, you'll probably find an option that fits. Once your results load, you'll see a surprisingly extensive list of filters. You can narrow properties by neighborhood, star and guest ratings, amenities, bed type, hotel brand and proximity to popular attractions. There are also filters for specific room offers, such as free cancellation or included breakfast. For example, when I searched for a stay in Paris, I could narrow my results to specific neighborhoods like the Champs-Élysées, Montmartre and the area around the Louvre. I could even filter by nearby attractions, such as the Arc de Triomphe or Palais Garnier. Search results show both the cash and points price for eligible cardholders. For example, the Hotel Du Louvre, Part Of Hyatt, was listed for $646 or 61,842 points plus $27. On the final booking page, BofA Travel breaks down the total price, including any taxes and fees or amounts due at the property. You can also review the room details and cancellation policy before continuing to payment. How to book rental cars through the Bank of America Travel Center To search for a rental car, enter your pickup and drop-off locations, dates and times, as well as the driver's age. Once your results load, you can filter by pickup location, rental agency, vehicle type and transmission. Eligible cardholders will see both the cash and points cost in the search results. In the searches I tried, that price stayed the same all the way through checkout. That's a nicer feature than it might sound. I've booked plenty of one-way rental cars where the drop-off fee wasn't shown during booking, or I wasn't even warned there would be one. Seeing that cost upfront makes it much easier to know what you'll actually pay. Before paying for your reservation, you can (and should) review the rental company's policies by opening the "Read agency policies" tab. This includes important information about age and payment requirements, deposits, insurance, additional drivers and other rental-specific rules. Cancellation and payment policies vary by reservation; for example, one rate I checked was nonrefundable, nontransferable and couldn't be changed. How to book activities through the Bank of America Travel Center Activities and experiences are available through the portal, too. Just search by city or attraction to see what's available. From there, you can browse tours, transportation, attractions, experiences, food and travel essentials. You can also filter results by price, star rating, duration and category or sort them by popularity, price or rating. Select an activity to see the available booking options and more detailed information, including departure and return details, what to expect, additional information and the cancellation policy. Pay attention to how each activity is priced. For example, the private Paris airport transfer I looked at was priced for up to two people rather than per person, and the displayed price included all taxes and fees. How to redeem rewards through the Bank of America Travel Center Eligible cardholders can redeem Bank of America rewards toward bookings through BofA Travel. You don't need enough rewards to cover the entire cost, either. You can pay with rewards, combine rewards with a credit or debit card or pay entirely by card. Bank of America says these redemption options vary by card and will expand over time. BofA Rewards points are worth at least 1 cent each when redeemed through BofA Travel. That means 50,000 points would cover at least $500 in flights, hotels, rental cars or activities. However, some cardholders can get even more value from their points. For example, the Premium Rewards Elite carries a hefty $550 annual fee, but if you're a frequent BofA Travel user, you can make up some ground with one particularly valuable perk: a 20% discount when redeeming points for airfare. For example, a $1,000 flight that would normally require 100,000 points costs just 80,000 points — a value of 1.25 cents per point. The discount also applies to the portion of airfare paid with points when you combine points and a card payment. Should you book through the Bank of America Travel Center? There are some good reasons to book through BofA Travel. But the portal won't make sense for every booking — and depending on how you travel, one of the best travel rewards credit cards from another issuer could potentially offer more value. When it makes sense to book through the BofA Travel Center Consider booking through BofA Travel when: - You want to redeem BofA Rewards points for travel. Eligible cardholders can use points toward flights, hotels, rental cars and activities, or combine points with a credit or debit card payment. - You have the Premium Rewards Elite card. Cardholders get a 20% points discount when redeeming rewards for airfare through BofA Travel. - Your card earns bonus rewards through the Travel Center. Some Bank of America cards offer elevated earning rates on eligible Travel Center purchases. - You're booking an independent hotel. You won't be giving up chain-specific hotel points, elite-night credits or elite benefits by booking through a third-party portal. - The price and booking terms are competitive. If BofA Travel has the same or a better price than booking directly, using the portal can make sense — especially if you're also earning bonus rewards or redeeming points. When booking directly may be better Before booking, do a quick price check with the airline, hotel or rental car company directly. BofA Travel won't always have the lowest rate, and there's no reason to spend more just to book through the portal. Be especially careful with chain hotels. Because BofA Travel is a third-party booking platform, you'll give up hotel points, elite-night credits and elite benefits by booking through the portal. An independent hotel, on the other hand, is a safer bet since you won't be sacrificing those loyalty perks. Finally, check the change and cancellation terms before paying. As I found while testing the portal, these can vary significantly by booking. Some reservations were nonrefundable, and some flights had to be managed directly with the airline after booking. Earning rewards on BofA Travel bookings The rewards you'll earn on BofA Travel bookings depend on which Bank of America card you use: - Bank of America Travel Rewards credit card: Earn 3 points per dollar spent on purchases made through the Travel Center. - Bank of America Premium Rewards credit card: Earn 2 points per dollar spent on travel purchases. - Bank of America Premium Rewards Elite credit card: Earn 2 points per dollar spent on travel purchases. - Bank of America Customized Cash Rewards credit card: Earn 3% cash back on eligible travel purchases if travel is your selected choice category, on up to $2,500 in combined choice category, grocery store and wholesale club purchases each quarter (then 1%; this card offers 6% back on your choice category in the first cardholder year, up to the aforementioned quarterly maximum). - Bank of America Unlimited Cash Rewards credit card: Earn unlimited 1.5% cash back on purchases. BofA Rewards™ can make these rates even better. Depending on your tier, you can get a 10% to 75% rewards bonus on eligible Bank of America cards. Bottom line BofA Travel may not get as much attention as other credit card travel portals, but there's plenty to like about the revamped booking experience. It's especially useful for Premium Rewards Elite cardholders, who get a 20% points discount on airfare. Just compare prices and booking terms before you book to make sure BofA Travel is the best option for your trip.

item.title: The 10 best places to travel in October 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.38
The 10 best places to travel in October 2026 Editor's Note October is one of the best months to plan a leisure trip. In many popular destinations, it's shoulder season, bringing fewer crowds, lower hotel rates and comfortable weather. In the Northern Hemisphere, it's also prime time for fall foliage, while destinations south of the equator are welcoming spring with blooming flowers and warming temperatures. From leaf-peeping in New England to wine tasting in Vienna and chasing hot air balloons in Japan, these are 10 of the best places to visit in the U.S. and beyond this October. Related: 9 cool hotels for leaf peeping, from Central Park to the Rocky Mountains Zürich, Switzerland In October, Zürich comes to life with fall colors, cultural events and seasonal experiences. A major highlight is the Zurich Film Festival, running from Sept. 24 to Oct. 4. The festival features more than 100 films and a packed lineup of talks, masterclasses and galas featuring filmmakers, actors and other international guests. Just outside the city, Jucker Farm hosts its annual Pumpkin Exhibition through Oct. 25. The family-friendly event features elaborate pumpkin sculptures based on this year's "Bon Voyage" theme, along with a food festival and immersive activities including fruit picking and an apple maze. Later in the month, Expovina Weinschiffe, taking place from Oct. 29 to Nov. 12, transforms the boats at Bürkliplatz into a floating wine fair. The event brings together wine producers and visitors for tastings aboard a fleet of ships overlooking Lake Zürich. Feeling more active? Head to Üetliberg, the mountain overlooking Zürich and just a short train ride from the city center. Its network of trails is especially appealing in autumn, when colorful foliage frames sweeping views of the city, Lake Zürich, and, on clear days, the Alps. TPG tip: Situated in the city's historic Old Town and spanning nine medieval townhouses, the upscale Widder Hotel features 49 unique rooms and suites with thoughtfully preserved details, including ancient frescoes and terracotta flooring. It is also home to the two-Michelin-starred Restaurant Widder, overseen by chef Stefan Heilemann. Nightly rates in October start at $910. Book a stay of two or more nights through American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts to receive daily breakfast for two guests, guaranteed late checkout and a $100 property credit to use on qualifying food and beverages. Asheville, North Carolina While we never need a reason to plan a vacation to Asheville, a visit is also a meaningful way to support the city as it continues to recover after Hurricane Helene. With cool events and festivals happening every day, October is one of the best times of the year to visit. LaZoom's Ghosted! Adult-only Haunted Comedy Tour (Oct. 1 to 31) is a humorous and educational tour aboard the company's signature purple buses. To see Biltmore in a whole new light, check out Luminere at Biltmore (Oct. 1 to 18), an outdoor evening experience that illuminates America's Largest Home and its famous gardens with dynamic visuals and sounds. Other October picks include the family-friendly, corn-themed Eliada Corn Maze and Festival (Oct. 1 to 31); the 369 Monologue and Short Play Festival (Oct. 1 to 18), a celebration of artists of color; and the Craft Fair of the Southern Highlands (Oct. 15 to 18), one of the country's top craft events. Some of the most picturesque spots to take in Asheville's majestic fall foliage include the Blue Ridge Parkway — the views are especially stunning at Black Balsam Knob and Craggy Gardens — as well as Looking Glass Falls and Biltmore Estate. Asheville's dining and drinking scene is unpretentious, but never short on quality. Botiwalla, by James Beard Award-winning chef Meherwan Irani, celebrates India's vibrant street food culture, while Mother turns out hearty sandwiches and sweets, including a cookie bar made with its long-fermented sourdough. For a proper nightcap and dessert, head to Potential New Boyfriend, a colorful, retro-styled lounge serving natural wines and indulgent, ever-rotating ice cream flavors. TPG Tip: Following a sweeping Hurricane Helene restoration, the stately Grand Bohemian Lodge Asheville reopened last year, with updates to its locally curated art program and steakhouse, Red Stag Grill. Rooms are available from $215 or 85,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October. The playful and conveniently located Moxy Asheville Downtown is also a great pick; nightly October rates start at $132 or 47,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. If glamping is your style, book the recently opened AutoCamp Asheville, with charming cabins and airstreams set on 16 scenic acres along the French Broad River. In October, accommodations are available from $256 or 70,000 Hilton Honors points per night. Related: The ultimate Blue Ridge Parkway road trip guide Saga, Japan If you want to visit Japan this fall while avoiding the biggest tourist crowds, consider Saga. This prefecture in northwestern Kyushu is gaining attention for its porcelain, sake and onsen culture — and October brings several can't-miss events. From Oct. 30 to Nov. 3, the Saga International Balloon Fiesta, Asia's largest sky sports event, fills the sky with colorful balloons, including some modeled after animals and cartoon characters. Cycling fans can also plan their trip around the 2026 Tour de Kyushu, an international road race that traverses six prefectures in Kyushu, including Saga on Oct. 10. Mild autumn weather is another draw, with daytime temperatures averaging in the mid-70s. And while Japan is already beloved for its world-class fall foliage, the season also brings a lesser-known but equally spectacular sight: peak cosmos blooms in red, white and pink. One of the best places to see them is Saga's Kinryu Park. TPG Tip: With just 84 rooms, Fairfield by Marriott Saga Ureshino Onsen offers an intimate, comfortable home base for exploring the region's legendary hot springs and rich culinary culture, including green tea and tofu. Rooms start at $78 per night or 17,000 Marriott Bonvoy points in October. Burlington, Vermont With its abundance of native trees (including sugar maples) and mountainous terrain, New England has long been one of the world's most cherished destinations for fall foliage. The catch, naturally, is the crush of crowds. This is where Burlington comes in. Set on the shores of Lake Champlain, Vermont's biggest city balances a small-town feel with urban conveniences — and, of course, spectacular scenery. Plus, the weather this time of year is blissful, averaging in the 50s. For optimal leaf-peeping, visit Centennial Woods, a 65-acre forest on the edge of the University of Vermont campus. For panoramic views of Lake Champlain, take a leisurely hike at Rock Point. Cycling enthusiasts can rent a bike from Local Motion and ride the Island Line Trail, which extends into Lake Champlain and offers spectacular views of the Adirondack Mountains. Burlington's culinary scene is tiny but mighty. The warm and deeply knowledgeable Kate Wise, a 2026 James Beard semifinalist, leads the lively bar at Hotel Vermont's Juniper Bar & Restaurant. Paul Trombly, a 2026 James Beard finalist for Best Chef: Northeast, sends out lovely, mostly plant-based dishes — order the crispy rice and lentil pancakes — at the cozy Fancy's. Fellow 2026 James Beard nominee for Outstanding Restaurateur Leslie Wells recently opened her fourth concept, Alimentari Café & Provisions. To make flying in and out even more comfortable, Leahy Burlington International Airport recently unveiled a $68 million, fossil-fuel-free expansion, complete with a brand-new terminal, more gates and additional amenities — all designed with sustainability in mind. TPG tip: With a prime address in downtown Burlington along Lake Champlain, The Harborvale debuted a few months ago with 161 guest rooms and suites in earthy tones, plus a namesake restaurant specializing in rustic, locally sourced fare. In October, nightly rates start at $274 or 55,000 Marriott Bonvoy points. Vienna If you're an art and culture lover, October is one of the best months to visit Austria's capital. But if you only have a weekend to spare, make it Oct. 3 to 4. This way, you can combine the final days of Vienna Design Week (Sept. 25 to Oct. 4) — one of Europe's top design festivals, celebrating its 20th anniversary this year — with the Long Night of Museums (Oct. 3), when a single ticket gives you access to museums and cultural institutions staying open late for one evening. It's also the opening weekend of the Vienna Drag Festival (Oct. 3 to18). Viennale (Oct. 22 to Nov. 3), Austria's premier international film festival, and Design District (Oct. 9 to 11), an annual showcase of interior design and furniture, are also worth checking out. As October is harvest season in the city's vineyards, set aside some time for wine-related experiences: sipping Wiener Gemischter Satz, Vienna's signature wine, at Heurigen (traditional wine taverns); hiking through the vineyards of Kahlenberg and Nussberg; and hopping aboard the Heurigen Express, a miniature train that loops through the city's wine-growing districts. In case you didn't know, Vienna is an under-the-radar destination for fall foliage. With approximately 1,000 parks and gardens, there are plenty of spots — local picks include the historic Schönbrunn Palace Gardens and the city parks of Stadtpark, Volksgarten and Burggarten — to immerse yourself in the seasonal scenery. TPG Tip: Housed in a beautifully restored 20th-century Art Nouveau building, Mandarin Oriental Vienna blends a posh, residential-style design with all the hallmarks the Hong Kong–based hospitality brand is known for: personalized service, a holistic approach to wellness — including Vienna's largest indoor pool — and elegant dining concepts that attract guests and locals alike. October rates for this American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts member start at $794 per night. Aruba Aruba lives up to its nickname, "One Happy Island," thanks to its consistently sunny weather, location outside the hurricane belt, cooling trade winds and silky beaches. No wonder it's such a popular year-round destination. If your travel dates are flexible, consider arriving during Aruba's low season in October. You'll enjoy lower hotel rates and fewer crowds while experiencing one of the island's biggest events: the Autentico Aruba Culinary Festival. Taking place Oct. 3 to 11, the festival celebrates the culinary traditions of the island's diverse population, reflecting its more than 100 nationalities. Highlights include special prix-fixe menus during Restaurant Week, chef-hosted Bucket List Experiences and the grand finale, The Pavilion. Other October events to mark on your calendar include the inaugural Leyenda del Dorado Aruba (Oct. 9 to 11), a three-day international mountain bike race across the island's craggy terrain, and Interpaso (Oct. 31 to Nov. 1), an international Paso Fino horse competition. Don't forget to pick up some of Aruba Aloe's world-famous skincare — perfect for soothing your sun-kissed skin and equally great for gift-giving — before you head home. TPG Tip: Based on the hotel-within-a-hotel concept, the new The Westerly at Hilton Aruba Caribbean Resort is an oceanfront tower with 161 crisp, airy rooms — the beds are especially dreamy — plus Terrace on 10, an adults-only rooftop retreat available for an additional fee. The indoor-outdoor space pairs stunning waterfront views with well-crafted drinks and all-day dining. Naturally, guests of The Westerly also have access to everything the Hilton resort has to offer, including the eforea Spa, casino and prime stretch of Palm Beach. Rooms are available from $743 or 243,000 Hilton Honors points per night in October. Lancaster County, Pennsylvania If you're after a scenic, culturally rich and delicious fall getaway — just a three-hour Amtrak ride from New York City — consider Lancaster County in south-central Pennsylvania. Home to the oldest and largest Amish community in the United States, the area is known for its bucolic landscape of rolling farmland, quiet streams and historic covered bridges. You'll likely find yourself sharing the road with Amish horse-drawn buggies, too. To learn more about Amish culture, visit the Amish Village, where an authentic 1840 farmhouse, one-room schoolhouse and other historic structures offer a glimpse into traditional Amish life. Opened in May in downtown Lancaster, the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center is a museum and educational center highlighting the lives and legacies of abolitionist and civil rights advocate Thaddeus Stevens and his partner, Lydia Hamilton Smith. Since 1954, Kitchen Kettle Village has grown into a charming destination in its own right, with more than 40 shops, including the iconic Jam & Relish Kitchen, Kling House Restaurant and residential-style accommodations. Lancaster County's restaurant scene offers an enticing mix of old and new. For casual bites, check out Lancaster Central Market, the oldest continuously operated public market in America, and Southern Market, just a few blocks away. Nathan Flaim, a 2026 James Beard Award finalist for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic, has grown Luca into a popular destination for exceptional housemade pastas and small plates that showcase Lancaster's rich bounty. Passerine and Vécu are equally charming brunch options, while Front Porch Baking Co. specializes in loaves and pastries baked with Pennsylvania-grown grains. No trip to Lancaster, however, would be complete without visiting a smorgasbord, a massive buffet including Pennsylvania Dutch comfort foods like potato filling, chicken corn soup and shoofly pie. TPG Tip: Taking up residence in the former Wilbur Chocolate Factory, the 74-key Wilbur Lititz, Tapestry Collection by Hilton retains many of the historic structure's original details — timber beams, exposed brick and arched windows — while incorporating modern touches, from the chocolate scent that infuses the lobby to Kōle Chophouse, a relaxed steakhouse serving Japanese Wagyu fired on a Josper charcoal grill. Nightly October rates start at $216 or 63,000 Hilton Honors points. Seychelles Though Seychelles makes for a great warm-weather vacation any time of year, October holds even more appeal for those seeking sublime weather — hot, sunny and relatively dry, with little wind or rain. The month is also ideal for catching big fish, such as barracuda and various tuna species. The island nation is also renowned for its diverse birdlife, and October provides an opportune time to spot migratory shorebirds like Pacific golden plovers and breeding seabirds, including sooty terns. The Creole Festival, an annual celebration of the archipelago's unique tapestry of African, European and Asian influences, will be hosted in the country's lively capital of Victoria during the last week of October. TPG tip: The all-villa Cheval Blanc Seychelles marks the sixth property in LVMH's swanky Cheval Blanc portfolio, and the first in Africa. Receive daily breakfast for two, late checkout and more when you book via the Amex Fine Hotels + Resorts program. Nightly rates in October start at $2,600. Puebla, Mexico Puebla is the antidote for those weary of touristy Mexico City and Tulum. Despite being Mexico's fourth-biggest city, Puebla balances everything you want from a well-rounded vacation destination — restaurants, shopping, history — with a neighborly, small-town feel. October is one of the best times to visit, as the month marks the transition from the rainy season to the dry season, with average daytime highs in the mid- to high 70s. Even better? It's easy to experience the best of Puebla in one weekend. Meander through the city's UNESCO-listed historic center, filled with colorful 16th- and 17th-century churches and other religious structures. As Puebla is the birthplace of mole poblano, the famously complex sweet-savory sauce, try as many versions as possible while you're in town. Some of the best can be found at the Michelin Guide-recommended Augurio, from beloved local chef Ángel Vázquez, as well as Comal and Mural de los Poblanos. It's also worth shopping for talavera, the region's colorful, hand-painted ceramics. TPG tip: A member of American Express Fine Hotels + Resorts, Banyan Tree Puebla is a 78-room property that celebrates Pueblan culture from its design to its offerings, including the highly recommended mole cooking class. Rooms in October start at $195 per night. Brisbane, Australia No longer hiding in the shadows of Sydney and Melbourne, Brisbane — Australia's third-largest city and Queensland's capital — has blossomed into a worldly yet laid-back destination. With pleasant October temperatures hovering in the mid- to high 70s, Brisbane is an urban paradise for outdoor lovers, whether you want to soak in the rays at Streets Beach (a unique human-made beach) or get up close to wildlife at Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary. The city's restaurant landscape has also been attracting attention, with the ambitious tasting-menu concept Exhibition, wood-fired Agnes and intimate August, housed in a refurbished 137-year-old heritage church, leading the charge. TPG tip: Since 2018, the W Brisbane has been one of the city's hippest places to hang your hat. Rooms are available from $360 or 48,000 Marriott Bonvoy points per night in October.

item.title: What's it like staying at Hyatt's new Caption branded hotels in Osaka and Tokyo
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.72
What's it like staying at Hyatt's new Caption branded hotels in Osaka and Tokyo One of World of Hyatt's newest brands is called Caption, and after a stay at two of only six properties worldwide, I can safely say it captured my heart. Hyatt describes the brand as "of the community," and that's definitely what they are going for at the two Caption hotels in Japan that I visited. I booked two nights in Tokyo and two nights in Osaka so that TPG could get a sense of the new brand and share with readers why they might want to choose these hotels in the heart of two of the country's largest cities. Related: The 11 best hotels in Tokyo for your next Japan getaway The best part of the stay? The price tag. Japan hotels can be notoriously expensive, but the Caption by Hyatt Namba Osaka and Kabutocho Tokyo were quite reasonable. I'd definitely recommend these hotels, especially if you are going to be mostly sightseeing during your stay. Here's a look at each property, how much it costs and why you might want to consider it on your next Japan adventure. Caption by Hyatt Kabutocho Tokyo I spent two nights at the Caption by Hyatt Kabutocho in Tokyo. The hotel opened late in 2025, so it's still looking brand-new and in tip-top shape. The building itself is made of a combination of wood and steel as part of a low-carbon structure, and there's an obvious and genuine effort toward sustainability. The hotel was even awarded Tokyo's first-ever DBJ Green Building Certification. Caption by Hyatt Kabutocho sits in an interesting location, within the city's business district. It's actually close to the Tokyo Stock Exchange, but it's not far from the famous shopping districts of Ginza and Nihombashi as well. There are several nearby subway lines, and Tokyo Station is about a five-minute taxi ride away. The hotel has 195 rooms, including one suite. I didn't bother asking for the suite, despite my Hyatt Globalist status, though the friendly receptionist who checked me in told me I'd been upgraded to a deluxe high-floor room. Non-suite rooms range from 269 to 301 square feet. Overall, the room was great — a bit on the small side, but no smaller than several other Tokyo Hyatt hotels that I've stayed in over the years. The bed was comfortable with a variety of fluffy and firm pillows. There were outlets throughout the room, including next to the bed on both sides. Views were fun, with sweeping city vistas and even a peek at Tokyo Tower off in the distance. A blackout curtain kept the light out with the pull of a beaded string. There was also a separate seating area with a small loveseat, a chair and a small desktop. A bulletin board had magnets and a notepad and a pen, and there were cute little signs throughout the room. There was also a pegboard with several shoe care accessories. I don't love the open-air concept closets, but it was fairly practical with a small ironing board and steamer, four drawers (one of which held a safe) and darling pajama sets. There was also a first for me: A humidifier in the room. There was a small fridge in a cabinet that also held a kettle and some glasses. On top of the cabinet was a pitcher (you can fill up on filtered water on every floor) and a small ice bucket. The bathroom was on the smaller side, but fine. There was a single sink and a walk-in shower. Apotheke amenities were available in large bottles. The water pressure was excellent, though there was only a wand showerhead. There was also a full Toto bidet toilet. There was also anything else you might need for free available at the check-in counter, including toothpaste, shave cream, moisturizer and even a packaged bath towel. On the second floor, there was a large living space where the hotel intended for folks to gather in a community style. I didn't see anyone in there any of the times I visited (that's where you'll find the ice machine). There was a small balcony there with city street views, but no outdoor seating. On the same floor, there was a decent-sized gym with plenty of brand-new Lifefitness equipment, including elliptical machines and treadmills, along with a small selection of free weights. The lobby was where most of the action was happening at the hotel. That's where meals were served all throughout the day, and it was always busy. It's a Caption signature space called "Talk Shop." The lobby looks at it like a communal space where everyone can escape their small rooms and hang out. There were multiple seating areas and lots of friendly staff manning the various counters and the check-in desks. I can see this being very popular, not only with the younger demographic Caption is targeting, but also with people who live in the nearby community. The hotel calls it a "lively, flexible space where a restaurant, coffee shop, bar and co-working space all come together." I got free breakfast both days of my stay as a World of Hyatt Globalist, but there is a set breakfast menu that will cost you between $17 and $20 depnding on your order. I tried a traditional Japanese breakfast one day and overnight oats on another. Both meals were delicious. The one thing that was a glaring omission in my book? There were no espresso drinks available. Drip coffee was all that was available during my stay. The most interesting tidbit of my stay was being awoken at 2 a.m. with an alert of an incoming earthquake on my phone. Moments later, the room was shaking quite hard. It was a 5.9 tremor. Enough to shake the room, but no damage, and the hotel didn't even make an announcement. Normal stuff in Japan, I guess. View this post on Instagram I stayed two nights at this Category 5 Hyatt property, where points bookings generally run 20,000 or 25,000 World of Hyatt points per night. Cash rates are much more reasonable here. I saw prices as low as $187 per night, though TPG paid $542 for two nights in the high summer season. Caption by Hyatt Namba Osaka I have similar positive things to say about my stay at Caption by Hyatt Nammba Osaka, but two additional things made it even better. First, the location. The 167-room Caption in Osaka is in the heart of the bustling Namba neighborhood with easy access to the incredible variety of street food and shopping that this wonderful neighborhood enjoys. Related: Hyatt's 1st Caption hotel is open: My time walking (and sleeping) in Memphis It was only a 15-minute walk to the world-famous Dotonbori Street with its flashing neon signs and shops selling everything from sushi to streetwear. This is also where you'll find the famous "running man" neon billboard. This is like the Times Square of Osaka. I loved it. The second standout feature was the laundry machines on the second floor. At this point in my two-week Asia trip, I was in desperate need of fresh laundry. The machines are coin-operated and a bit pricey, but it was so nice to have clean clothes. I spent about $8 on a load of laundry (detergent is included, and the machine fills automatically). Despite being in a noisy neighborhood, the new construction of the Caption meant there was no noise at night, allowing for a great night's sleep. Though my queen-sized bed was a bit firm, I still slept well. The 10th-floor room was on the small side, but it did have a separate seating area with two chairs. City views were charming, and blackout curtains worked well here, too. Like the Caption in Tokyo, outlets were plentiful, and there was fun pop art throughout the room. Check out the samurai sword clothing rack in the open-air closet. The bathroom was tiny but had a Toto bidet toilet and a shower with both a wand and a rainhead, with excellent water pressure. Just like at the Tokyo hotel, there was a gym, but that was really it for major amenities. It was on the smaller side, but I did manage to use some of the free weights. The main floor held the lobby and the signature Talk Shop. The space was huge, even when filled with stored luggage. I enjoyed a Western-style breakfast. There were plenty of seating areas, including a large outdoor space (though it was too hot to try while I was there). Interestingly, both hotels had self-check-in machines, but the front desks were always fully staffed with friendly employees, and I didn't see anyone actually using them to check in. I paid just $234.95 for two nights at this Category 3 property. I'd call that a great deal, but you can also book it for as few as 8,000 World of Hyatt points per night. Cash rates are as low as $99 a night, but more often around $129. It's the only Hyatt option in Osaka for World of Hyatt fans. Both hotels were fully wheelchair accessible, with some ADA-compliant rooms. Elevators were accessible with grab bars, Braille signage and lowered buttons. Bottom line I'd happily stay at both the Hyatt Kabutocho Tokyo and the Caption by Hyatt Namba Osaka again anytime. The relaxed vibes and quiet, comfortable rooms are all you need for a stay in the big cities when what you'll mostly be doing is sightseeing anyway. Central locations make visiting the city easy, with subways and even some major attractions a short walk away. While the lack of a long list of amenities will put some people off, the budget-friendly bill at the end of the stay makes these properties shine. Related reading: - Ocean oasis: A review of the Andaz Maui at Wailea Resort in Hawaii - World of Hyatt gold: What it's really like to stay at the Andaz Munich Schwabinger Tor - I didn't expect to love World of Hyatt, but here's why I do - What it's like staying at the Park Hyatt New York — a gorgeous flagship property bookable on points

item.title: Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.59
Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it? Editor's Note If you fly American Airlines frequently, you may want to consider getting one of its cobranded Citi cards. At the top of the hierarchy is the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees), which offers the most AA-specific perks of any credit card. The card recently underwent a significant refresh in August, which raised the annual fee to $695 but also added substantial new benefits. Doing the math on this card is now more important than ever — but there's also more value to potentially unlock if you maximize each of the new perks. So, is it worth the annual fee — both in year one and beyond? Let's do the math. Welcome bonus New Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard cardholders can currently earn a limited time offer of 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. This bonus is worth about $1,813, based on TPG's September 2026 valuations, and is the highest we've seen on the card, so now is the best time to apply. This bonus accounts for a significant portion of the card's overall value, so earning it and redeeming the miles wisely are crucial to offsetting the card's high annual fee. Related: The Citi / AAdvantage Executive's new benefits are live: 6 things to do now Lounge access Arguably, the most valuable ongoing benefit of this card is the complimentary Admirals Club membership you'll receive every year that you hold it. When you have the Citi / AA Executive, all you have to do is walk to the lounge and present a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight. An annual membership costs $750 to $1,400, depending on your status level and whether you want access only to AA-branded lounges or to partner lounges as well. Given that this card carries a $695 annual fee, it doesn't make sense to buy an Admirals Club membership on its own, unless you aren't eligible for the card. With this card, you'll be able to access almost 50 Admirals Clubs and more than 60 partner lounges worldwide when flying American or one of its Oneworld partners. Notably, this includes Alaska Lounges in hubs like Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Portland International Airport (PDX), San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA). You can bring in either your immediate family members (spouse or domestic partner and children under 18 years of age) or up to two guests. And they don't need to be on the same flight as you — just any American or Oneworld flight with a same-day boarding pass. Related: The best lounge access credit cards to add to your wallet Travel benefits The Citi / AA Executive offers valuable perks when flying American, including priority check-in at business-class counters (where available) and priority boarding privileges (where available) for you and up to eight travelers on the same reservation. You also get your first checked bag free on domestic itineraries with American Airlines, saving you at least $45 each time. (Note that this is only for domestic flights; I had to pay out of pocket when I traveled to Mexico, forgetting the restrictions of this perk.) Additionally, you'll receive a statement credit of up to $120 for Global Entry/TSA PreCheck. (I suggest maximizing your credit by applying for Global Entry, as it includes PreCheck anyway.) You'll also receive elite status with two partner programs: - Omni Champion, which includes room upgrades, early check-in and late checkout privileges (subject to availability), and an annual free night reward after qualifying stays at participating Omni Hotels properties. - Avis President's Club (through Aug. 31, 2028), providing car rental upgrades (subject to availability), the ability to skip the rental counter at major airports and complimentary additional drivers. Furthermore, the card includes travel protections, such as trip cancellation, trip interruption, trip delay, lost baggage protection and car rental insurance coverage. And there are no foreign transaction fees, making this card a good option for international purchases. Related: Which airline is now best if you don't want to pay bag fees? Elite status If chasing AAdvantage elite status is important to you, the Citi / AA Executive will help you achieve it. You'll earn 1 Loyalty Point for every mile you earn from purchases. Cardholders also earn 10,000 bonus Loyalty Points after reaching each of the following milestones in the same status qualification year: - 50,000 Loyalty Points - 90,000 Loyalty Points - 165,000 Loyalty Points - 240,000 Loyalty Points Related: 8 methods that earned American AAdvantage Executive Platinum Statement credits The statement credits on the Citi / AA Executive include: - Up to $500 in annual American Airlines Vacations statement credits (up to $250 every six months) - Up to $180 in annual Lyft credits ($15 monthly) — but you have to take three eligible rides each month first to receive this credit - Up to $120 back in statement credits on eligible prepaid rentals booked directly on Avis.com or Budget.com every calendar year - Up to $100 annual statement credit for eligible American Airlines inflight and Admirals Club purchases The American Airlines Vacations credits are only valuable if you'd book these packages anyway. Note that the credit splits into two $250 six-month periods — you must use one in the first half of the year and one in the second; unused credits don't roll over. Qualifying packages typically require at least two travel components (flight plus hotel, flight plus rental car, etc.), though you can often minimize costs by adding a cheap rental car to a flight or hotel booking. I've had issues with the car rental credit, so I wouldn't rely on it for value. Previously, a Budget rental in Cabo was not coded correctly, and Citi wouldn't manually apply the credit. Later, I completed another Budget rental in Ireland and waited the obligatory 10 weeks. Again, it didn't post, and again, Citi refused to apply a manual credit. I don't value the Lyft perk because you don't get the $15 credit until after you've taken three (non-discounted) rides in a month. Instead, I use my Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) to earn 5 points per dollar spent, plus a $10 monthly in-app credit on Lyft purchases (through Sept. 30, 2027). The inflight (and Admirals Club) credit is useful if you regularly buy onboard refreshments or snacks. Related: Frequent Uber or Lyft user? These are the best credit cards for you Earning and redeeming miles If you're looking to supercharge your points earning across several programs, I'd suggest putting your spending on a card that earns transferable points. However, if you want to maximize your AAdvantage mile balance specifically, the Citi / AA Executive will earn you: - 12 miles per dollar spent on eligible car rentals and hotels booked through American's car rental and hotel booking sites, respectively - 4 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases (jumps to 5 miles per dollar spent for the remainder of the calendar year once you've spent $150,000 on purchases in a calendar year) - 1 mile per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases AAdvantage miles are more valuable (at 1.45 cents each) than United MileagePlus miles (1.2 cents) and Delta SkyMiles (1.2 cents), according to our valuations. I redeemed part of the welcome bonus I received on this card for a luxurious flight. I used 70,000 miles plus $174 for a one-way business-class flight in Qatar Airways' fantastic Qsuite from Doha to Houston. Given that this flight retails for $3,910 one-way, I got a very high 5.6 cents per mile from this redemption, quadruple TPG's valuation of AAdvantage miles. Related: The best uses of American Airlines AAdvantage miles Authorized users Finally, the Citi / AA Executive is a great option if you want to extend Admirals Club access to friends and family affordably. You can add up to three authorized users for $175 total (about $58 each), and $175 each after that. Each authorized user receives Admirals Club access (with a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight) for themselves and up to two traveling companions. However, authorized users only get Admirals Club access, not a full Admirals Club membership. Related: Everything you need to know about authorized credit card users Bottom line Ultimately, if you value Admirals Club access, priority perks on American flights and a large welcome bonus, this card can easily justify its fee. You'll get even more value if you take advantage of its statement credits and authorized user perks. But if lounge access isn't important to you, consider one of Citi's lower-fee AAdvantage cards instead. To learn more, read our full review of the Citi / AA Executive World Legend Mastercard. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |
